The After-Action Report gives more than 850 people injured, including first responders.
properties.verification_note: From a summary, not read at source.

evidence.note: From a summary, not read at source.

title: More than 900 rounds into the crowd (NYT analysis)

properties.statement: The New York Times counted more than 900 rounds fired into the crowd, from audio across 30 videos.
properties.verification_note: Counts only the rounds heard into the crowd.

evidence.note: Counts only the rounds heard into the crowd.

properties.statement: The gunfire into the crowd came in twelve main bursts (volleys). The NYT identified them from 30 videos; the map numbers volleys 1 to 12.
properties.verification_note: The NYT and the map agree. The map may follow the NYT numbering, which is not known; the sync check shows the map's own annotations cluster into 12 separate times.

evidence.note: The NYT and the map agree. The map may follow the NYT numbering, which is not known; the sync check shows the map's own annotations cluster into 12 separate times.

title: Three intervals of more than a minute between bursts

properties.statement: Between the twelve bursts there were three intervals of more than one minute.
properties.verification_note: Checked against the map in sync-check.md.

evidence.note: Checked against the map in sync-check.md.

title: One burst of about 40 seconds below the gunman's position

properties.statement: A burst of about 40 seconds appears in footage filmed directly below the gunman's position but not in simultaneous festival recordings, which suggests gunfire inside the building. The map's 'down-the-hall' annotations may be the same event; that is not established.
properties.verification_note: From the reporter's thread; no clock time is given.

evidence.note: From the reporter's thread; no clock time is given.

title: When the hotel security guard was shot

properties.statement: The NYT analysis places the shooting of the hotel security guard at about 10:06 p.m., one minute into the attack, which differed from the investigators' timeline of the time. The official time is not carried until the reports are read.
properties.verification_note: The official timeline was revised more than once in October 2017. From summaries only.

evidence.note: The official timeline was revised more than once in October 2017. From summaries only.

title: No six-minute gap in the timeline (police, 13 October 2017)

properties.statement: On 13 October 2017 police said there was no six-minute gap between the first shots and the concert shooting (headline of the Philadelphia Inquirer).
properties.verification_note: Headline wording; the article was not read.

evidence.note: Headline wording; the article was not read.
